subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Disruptive selection differs from the other types because it:
options: Favours the mean phenotype
Acts only on sex-linked genes
Reduces all variation
Favours both extreme phenotypes at the expense of intermediates
questions.explain: Disruptive selection favours both extremes and selects against intermediate phenotypes, potentially leading to two distinct groups.

questions.q: In a population at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 1 in 100 individuals is homozygous recessive. The frequency of the recessive allele (q) is:
questions.explain: q squared = 0.01, so q = the square root of 0.01 = 0.1.

questions.q: The R-group (variable side chain) of an amino acid is significant because it:
options: links nucleotides together
determines the chemical properties and interactions that shape tertiary structure
forms the peptide bond between amino acids
is identical in all 20 amino acids
questions.explain: The R-group varies between amino acids and its charge, polarity or ability to form disulfide bonds dictates folding and protein function.

questions.q: Why is glycogen a more suitable storage molecule than cellulose in animal cells?
options: Its glycosidic bonds cannot be hydrolysed
It contains beta-glucose, which is more soluble
It is unbranched and so packs tightly into fibres
It is highly branched, giving many free ends for rapid hydrolysis
questions.explain: Glycogen's highly branched structure provides many terminal glucose units, allowing rapid enzymatic release of glucose to meet metabolic demand.

questions.q: Why is starch an effective storage molecule in plants but unsuitable as the main respiratory substrate transported in solution?
options: It is insoluble and compact so it does not affect water potential, but this also makes it unsuitable for transport
It is highly soluble and so leaks out of cells
It is too small to store energy
It cannot be hydrolysed to glucose
questions.explain: Starch's insolubility means it has no osmotic effect and stores compactly, but the same property makes it unsuitable for transport, where soluble sucrose is used instead.

questions.q: Ribosomes found free in the cytoplasm of a eukaryotic cell are:
options: made of pure protein with no RNA
70S, the same as in the mitochondrion's matrix
80S, larger than the 70S ribosomes of prokaryotes
bound only to the rough endoplasmic reticulum
questions.explain: Eukaryotic cytoplasmic ribosomes are 80S, whereas prokaryotic and organellar ribosomes are the smaller 70S type.

questions.q: Modern classification places organisms into three domains. These are:
options: Monera, Protista and Eukarya
Plantae, Animalia and Fungi
Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya
Prokaryota, Protista and Eukaryota
questions.explain: The three-domain system divides life into Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya based largely on rRNA sequence differences.

questions.q: Courtship behaviour is important in evolution and classification because it:
options: Prevents all reproduction
Removes recessive alleles
Allows members of the same species to recognise each other and ensures reproductive isolation between species
Increases mutation rates
questions.explain: Species-specific courtship allows recognition of conspecific mates and maintains reproductive isolation between species.

questions.q: The Hardy-Weinberg principle predicts that allele and genotype frequencies remain constant only if:
options: The population is small with frequent migration
There is no mutation, no selection, no migration, random mating and a large population
Mating is non-random
Selection strongly favours one allele
questions.explain: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium assumes a large population with no mutation, selection or migration and random mating.

questions.q: A transmission electron microscope (TEM) differs from a scanning electron microscope (SEM) in that the TEM:
options: can be used on living specimens
produces a 3D surface image
passes electrons through a thin specimen to give a high-resolution 2D image of internal structure
has lower resolution than the SEM
questions.explain: A TEM transmits electrons through an ultra-thin section, producing a detailed 2D image of internal ultrastructure, whereas an SEM gives a 3D surface view.

questions.q: The standard hierarchy of taxonomic ranks, from largest to smallest, is:
options: Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum, Kingdom, Domain
Kingdom, Domain, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Domain, Phylum, Kingdom, Class, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Domain, Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
questions.explain: The accepted order is Domain, Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.q: In the DNA double helix, the two antiparallel strands are joined by:
options: hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs
phosphodiester bonds between complementary bases
ester bonds between sugars
peptide bonds between phosphates
questions.explain: Complementary bases (A-T, G-C) pair via hydrogen bonds; phosphodiester bonds instead link nucleotides along each strand.

questions.q: ATP is resynthesised from ADP and inorganic phosphate in a reaction that is:
options: a hydrolysis releasing energy
a condensation requiring energy, catalysed by ATP synthase
an oxidation of glucose
a spontaneous exergonic process needing no enzyme
questions.explain: Phosphorylation of ADP is an endergonic condensation reaction catalysed by ATP synthase, storing energy in the new phosphate bond.

questions.q: A phospholipid differs from a triglyceride in that a phospholipid has:
options: one fatty acid replaced by a phosphate-containing hydrophilic group
only ester bonds and no hydrophilic region
three fatty acids attached to glycerol
no glycerol backbone
questions.explain: In a phospholipid, one of the three fatty acids of a triglyceride is replaced by a hydrophilic phosphate group, making the molecule amphipathic.

questions.q: Stabilising selection acts to:
options: Increase the mutation rate
Favour both extremes against the mean
Favour one extreme phenotype
Favour the intermediate (mean) phenotype and reduce variation
questions.explain: Stabilising selection favours the mean phenotype, selecting against extremes and reducing variation.

questions.q: Sympatric speciation in plants can arise rapidly through polyploidy because polyploid offspring:
options: Are always sterile
Have fewer chromosomes
Reproduce only asexually
Cannot interbreed with the diploid parent population, creating instant reproductive isolation
questions.explain: Polyploids cannot produce fertile offspring with diploid parents, instantly isolating them reproductively.

questions.q: ATP is described as the universal energy currency because:
options: it stores energy long-term like glycogen
it cannot be regenerated once hydrolysed
hydrolysis of its terminal phosphate releases a manageable quantity of energy for cellular reactions
its hydrolysis releases a large, fixed amount of energy in a single immediate step
questions.explain: ATP releases a small, usable amount of energy when its terminal phosphate bond is hydrolysed to ADP and Pi, and is rapidly resynthesised.

questions.q: The total magnification of a light microscope using a x10 eyepiece and a x40 objective lens is:
options: x4
questions.explain: Total magnification is the product of the eyepiece and objective magnifications: 10 multiplied by 40 = 400.

questions.q: In differential centrifugation of a cell homogenate, the order in which organelles sediment as speed increases is:
options: all organelles sediment together at the same speed
nuclei, then mitochondria/chloroplasts, then endoplasmic reticulum, then ribosomes
ribosomes first because they are densest
ribosomes, then mitochondria, then nuclei
questions.explain: The densest, largest organelles (nuclei) sediment first at low speeds; progressively smaller, less dense organelles pellet at higher speeds, with ribosomes last.

questions.q: Cell fractionation to isolate organelles requires the tissue to be placed in a solution that is cold, buffered and isotonic. The solution must be isotonic to:
options: denature enzymes that might digest organelles
prevent organelles bursting or shrinking due to osmotic water movement
speed up respiration
maintain a low pH
questions.explain: An isotonic solution has the same water potential as the organelles, preventing osmotic gain or loss of water that would damage them.

questions.q: Natural selection leads to evolution because:
options: Alleles that increase survival and reproduction become more frequent over generations
Individuals change their genes during their lifetime to suit the environment
All individuals reproduce equally
Mutations are always beneficial
questions.explain: Differential survival and reproduction of advantageous alleles increases their frequency in the gene pool over time.

questions.q: Collagen is a strong structural protein because:
options: three polypeptide chains wind into a triple helix held by hydrogen bonds, with staggered cross-links between molecules
it is a globular protein with a hydrophilic exterior
it consists of a single alpha-helix
it dissolves readily in water to form an enzyme
questions.explain: Collagen's three chains form a tight triple helix and adjacent molecules are covalently cross-linked in a staggered array, giving high tensile strength.

questions.q: In telophase of mitosis:
options: chromatids are pulled to opposite poles
chromosomes line up at the equator
chromosomes condense and the nuclear envelope breaks down
chromosomes decondense and two new nuclear envelopes form around the separated chromosomes
questions.explain: Telophase sees the separated chromosomes reach the poles, decondense, and become enclosed by re-formed nuclear envelopes before cytokinesis.

questions.q: The quaternary structure of haemoglobin refers to:
options: the sequence of amino acids in each chain
the alpha-helical coiling of a single chain
the association of four polypeptide subunits each with a haem prosthetic group
the folding of one polypeptide into a 3D shape
questions.explain: Quaternary structure is the arrangement of multiple polypeptide subunits; haemoglobin has four chains, each bound to a haem group.

questions.q: Reproductive isolation is essential for speciation because it:
options: Increases mutation rates
Removes natural selection
Prevents gene flow between diverging populations so they accumulate genetic differences
Forces all individuals to interbreed
questions.explain: Without gene flow, populations diverge genetically until they can no longer interbreed, becoming separate species.

questions.q: Glycogen and amylose both store glucose, but glycogen is more highly branched. A direct consequence of this branching is that glycogen:
options: contains beta-glucose monomers
is less soluble in water
forms straight chains that pack into fibres
can be hydrolysed more rapidly because of more terminal glucose residues
questions.explain: More branch points give more free ends from which glucose can be released quickly, suiting the high metabolic rate of animals.

questions.q: An organelle measured as 4.4 micrometres long appears 22 mm long in an electron micrograph. The magnification of the image is:
options: x5
questions.explain: Magnification = image size / actual size = 22000 micrometres / 4.4 micrometres = 5000.

questions.q: The genetic code is described as 'degenerate'. This means that:
options: Each codon codes for more than one amino acid
The code differs between organisms
Some codons do not code for any amino acid
Most amino acids can be coded for by more than one codon
questions.explain: Degeneracy means most amino acids are specified by more than one triplet codon.

questions.q: Which of the following is a prezygotic reproductive isolating mechanism?
options: Differences in courtship behaviour preventing mating
Death of the hybrid embryo
Hybrid breakdown in later generations
Hybrid sterility
questions.explain: Behavioural (courtship) isolation prevents mating, acting before a zygote can form, so it is prezygotic.

questions.q: In the Hardy-Weinberg equations, q squared represents the frequency of:
options: Homozygous recessive individuals
Heterozygous individuals
The recessive allele
The dominant allele
questions.explain: q squared is the frequency of the homozygous recessive genotype, since q is the recessive allele frequency.
